clue.text: Flounder, perhaps, if time cut back into fraction of second

indicators.note: the reversed letters are cut into the middle of the word for a brief instant

parts.note: a flash is an instant, a tiny fraction of a second

indicators.note: back tells us the letters of the words if and time are read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone dismissively wondering whether a struggling effort can be cut short within a split second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' looks like a verb (struggle), but it is the fish. 'back' turns the letters of 'if time' round to TFI, and 'cut ... into' places them within the split-second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The flounder is one example of a flat-bodied fish lying on the seabed, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: New student more open about librarian's request

indicators.note: the longer word is placed around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: freer means more open, less restricted
sh is the hushing sound a librarian makes asking for quiet

explanation.surface: A new undergraduate is more relaxed about the library's request for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: First-year university students are called freshers in British colleges.

clue.text: Positive response I read out

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the letter is pronounced like a word of assent

parts.note: the pronoun I

explanation.surface: Someone answering yes while reading something out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye is a dialect or parliamentary word for yes.

clue.text: Such stories are composed with falsity, perhaps

definitions.text: Such stories are composed with falsity, perhaps

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A claim that certain stories are made up of falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: these stories are made up, so the anagram of ARE + FALSITY also describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's fantasy tales about magic creatures are untrue by nature.

clue.text: Whichever way you look at it, the end of Socrates

definitions.text: Whichever way you look at it, the end of Socrates

parts.words: Whichever way you look at it, the end of Socrates
parts.note: the philosopher's name finishes with S in English, and with the Greek letter for S when written in Greek

explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of Socrates' sounds like his death by hemlock, but it is his last letter, S in either alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter for s ends the philosopher's name in its own alphabet.

clue.text: Awards zero marks as result of cuts

parts.note: the digit zero looks like the letter O
scars are the marks left on skin once wounds heal

explanation.surface: A teacher giving nought marks after cuts to the budget.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscars are the annual film prizes of the American Academy, so the word stands for awards.

clue.text: Whole ring used for wrestling

parts.note: a sum is a whole amount, a total
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: An entire ring set aside for a wrestling bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling between heavyweight competitors.

clue.text: Going into space makes one nervous

definitions.text: Going into space makes one nervous

parts.words: Going into space makes one nervous
parts.note: suggests astronauts, but 'space' means open places, and the person described fears going outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: 'space' suggests outer space; it means open areas, from the Greek agora, a market square.
explanation.definitionFit: This describes someone with a phobia of open or public places.

clue.text: Does it improperly secure first in race?

definitions.text: Does it improperly secure first in race?

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the jumbled letters hold another inside
improperly means wrongly, so these letters are set out in the wrong order
the opening letter of the word race

explanation.surface: A suspicious question: does this drug unfairly win first place in a race?
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly' turns DOES IT into STEOID, and 'secure' puts R, from 'first in race', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A banned performance-enhancing drug may be used by cheating athletes to win.

clue.text: Something man made after dreadful deed

indicators.note: dreadful means terrible, so the letters of the word after are badly rearranged

parts.note: an act is a deed, something done

explanation.surface: An object a man created following some terrible act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a time word placing the man's making later than the deed, but it is fodder; 'dreadful' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object crafted by humans, such as a tool or ornament.

clue.text: Improves green in variegated plant

indicators.note: variegated means streaked with mixed colours, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: a variegated plant brightens up a green lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variegated' looks like a description of the plant's leaves, but it signals rearranging the fifteen letters of IMPROVES GREEN IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening primrose is a yellow-flowered garden species whose blooms open at dusk.

clue.text: Writer holding a pair of kings

parts.note: Henry and James are both names borne by several English kings
Henry and James are both names borne by several English kings

explanation.surface: A card player's hand: a novelist holding a pair of kings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a poker hand; instead name two monarchs, Henry and James, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was the American-born novelist who wrote The Turn of the Screw.

clue.text: How one may be called to fight in France

definitions.text: How one may be called to fight in France

parts.words: How one may be called to fight in France
parts.note: read literally, the French phrase is a 'war name', the name a soldier might take when called up

explanation.walkthrough: 'called to fight' suggests conscription, but 'called' means named.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym adopted by a writer or fighter is a French phrase meaning 'war name'.

clue.text: Overhead lighting

parts.note: read literally: a ring of light seen above someone's head, as in religious paintings of saints

explanation.definitionFit: A saint's nimbus is a glowing circle painted above the head.

clue.text: Projectile making clergyman cry audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so we want words that sound the same as the clue's

parts.note: a canon is a cathedral clergyman and to bawl is to cry loudly

explanation.surface: A clergyman weeping noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy round iron shot fired from an old gun is a projectile.

clue.text: Kind of robbery led by Jason?

definitions.text: Kind of robbery led by Jason?

parts.words: Kind of robbery led by Jason?
parts.note: Jason led the Argonauts on an expedition to seize the Golden Fleece, the wool of a magic sheep, so his voyage was a raid for a male sheep

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Jason's quest was for the fleece of a golden male sheep; read that way his expedition was a raid for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram raid is a smash-and-grab theft where a vehicle is driven through a shop window.

clue.text: In warehouse, son in charge is domineering

indicators.note: the son goes in the warehouse, placed within it

parts.note: a depot is a storage warehouse

explanation.surface: The son running the warehouse is a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrannical ruler behaves in an overbearing, controlling way.

clue.text: Tree in one part of garden having turned red?

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

indicators.note: the tree's name goes in, within the patch of garden

parts.note: a bed is a plot of soil where flowers are grown
the ash is a common European tree

explanation.surface: A tree planted in a corner of the garden that has gone red in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned red' looks like autumn leaves, but it is the definition: someone embarrassed blushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed blushes, so going pink in the face suggests shame, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Woman from other place looks over French art

indicators.note: over here means placed across, with the outer word covering the French word

parts.note: peers means looks closely
es is the French for 'art', as in the old English 'thou art' (tu es)

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad studies French art closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other place' is the Commons' name for the House of Lords, where peers sit; the clue looks like it means a foreign woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled noblewoman can sit in the House of Lords, which members of the Commons call the 'other place'.

clue.text: Meat product swallowed by gull

definitions.meaning: a pastry case filled with chopped pork
in rhyming slang a 'porky pie' or ... is a lie, which a gull (a gullible person) swallows

explanation.walkthrough: 'gull' looks like the seabird eating food, but it means a dupe; Cockney rhyming slang is a British habit where pork pie stands for lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury pastry filled with pork, and a falsehood, from rhyming slang (pork pie = lie) which a dupe believes.

clue.text: Depleted football team's fit, okay as regards defence

parts.note: a football side has eleven players, so one short of that is ten
fit means capable, able

explanation.surface: A football side short of players is still fit enough to defend well.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be held or defended against attack or argument.

clue.text: Attempted piece of writing, limited edition

parts.note: an essay is a short written composition
ED is a shortened form of edition

explanation.surface: Someone trying for a limited edition of a written piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' looks like part of 'limited edition', but it says the word edition is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to try it, so essayed means tried.

clue.text: Libertine last to leave French city

indicators.note: the final letter of the city's name departs

parts.note: Rouen is a city in Normandy, northern France

explanation.surface: A rake is the last person to leave a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: A roué is a debauched man given to pleasure, a rake.

clue.text: This astronomer worked with pure conics

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters were worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A stargazer who studied pure conic sections, as mathematicians do.
explanation.definitionFit: Copernicus was the Polish scholar who put the sun at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: Become running mates

parts.note: suggests political candidates on a joint ticket, but means a couple running away together to marry

explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off secretly to wed become partners in flight.

clue.text: English poet a bit gloomy for the Americans

definitions.meaning: Thomas ... wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

definitions.text: a bit gloomy for the Americans
definitions.meaning: the US spelling of the colour between black and white, describing dull weather

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray wrote the famous Elegy; and the American spelling of a dull, overcast colour.

clue.text: Novel picture of 18 ac

parts.note: a portrait is a painted picture of a person
taken as written
the answer to 18 across is a woman of noble rank, so a lady

explanation.surface: A painting of the noblewoman from 18 across.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a novel by Henry James (11 across) about Isabel Archer.

clue.text: Fire weapon that can bring down plane

definitions.meaning: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

definitions.text: weapon that can bring down plane
definitions.meaning: a plane is also a kind of tree, which a chopping tool can fell

explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft shot down, but it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack an employee; and a chopping tool that can fell a plane tree.

clue.text: Diarist regularly writing name at end

indicators.note: the letter for name is written again at the end of the word

parts.note: evenly means regularly, at a steady rate

explanation.surface: A diarist who writes daily, always signing his name at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the usual abbreviation for name; take it out of EVENLY and put it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn was a seventeenth-century English diarist, contemporary with Samuel Pepys.

clue.text: Two English authors, both mostly very literate

indicators.note: each of the two names loses its final letter, so most of both remains

parts.note: H. G. Wells and Charles Reade were both English novelists
H. G. Wells and Charles Reade were both English novelists

explanation.surface: Two English writers who are both very literate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both mostly' cuts the last letter from each surname: WELLS gives WELL and READE gives READ.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has done much reading is knowledgeable about books.
